title: Grateful Dead Live at St. Paul Auditorium on 1973-02-17
lineage: DAT/0 (Tascam DA-40) > Tascam DA-3000 > Samplitude Pro X5 Suite > FLAC
source: SBD > Reel Master (7.5ips 1/2trk) > Reel/1 (7.5ips/Dolby B) > DAT/0 (Panasonic SV-3800/48k)

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a legendary 1973 Saint Paul show, featuring blazing Jerry solos, fiery Phil bass, and the iconic Help‑China‑Rider sandwich.
ai_review.review: Both reviewers rave about this February 1973 performance, calling it a “sweet spot” for the year with perfect song selection and fire‑hot playing. The Miller‑enhanced soundboard source is praised as crisp and upgraded, while the musical highlights—Phil’s burning bass driving Jerry’s white‑hot runs, a Dark Star tease, a monster Truckin’ opener, and an unforgettable Help on the Way → China Cat Sunflower → The Rider sandwich—make this a top‑tier Dead concert.

ai_rating.rationale: Both reviews give 5 stars and detail superb performance plus an upgraded soundboard, indicating an outstanding show and recording.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Miller’s upgrade yields a clean, crisp mix with no noted flaws; listeners appreciate the professional soundboard clarity.

standout_songs: Help on the Way > China Cat Sunflower > The Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds to a powerful closing, highlighted by Phil’s fire‑hot bass and Jerry’s soaring runs; second set opens with a strong Truckin’ and delivers a monumental jam culminating in the celebrated HCS→China→Rider sequence.

band_member_comments.Jerry: White‑hot runs praised throughout; his solo on Help on the Way described as near out‑of‑body.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as “on fire,” driving Jerry’s improvisations and energizing the band.
